Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Sentence (English): It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range.
Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.
