Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Comments (English): [ Buy a 12-seater media dishwasher instead of a 6-seater. ] || ---------------- || The reason I bought the 12-seater Media was because I live alone and mostly order delivery. I don't cook much, so I don't need a large capacity. I don't wash a lot of dishes, but I hate doing them, so I let them pile up for 3-4 days, then do them all at once on the weekends. It's unsanitary, and washing them on weekends makes me feel exhausted and like I haven't rested even when I'm resting. So, I decided to buy a 6-seater that I could use every day. However, the prices of 6-seater models have gone up since I looked a few months ago, with Cuckoo models ranging from 400,000 won to Samsung models ranging from 600,000 won. Furthermore, my sink is small, so I need to buy a dishwasher cabinet (average price: 200,000 won). All in all, I expected to spend 600,000-800,000 won. Until then, I'd never considered the 6-seater Media, even if it was cheaper. I wanted a familiar brand. For that price, I'd rather buy an LG 12-seater for around 700,000 won, which I thought would offer better cleaning power and allow me to handle larger pots. I looked into it, but it was a built-in model, lacking a drying function or a timer. My house doesn't allow built-in models, so I can only use a freestanding model. I started looking into freestanding models again, but they're 10-20% more expensive than built-in models and don't have as many features as the latest models. I don't wash a lot of dishes, and the price kept going up beyond my initial budget, so I decided this wasn't for me. Then I found a Media 12-seater on sale for 300,000 won! Because it's freestanding, I don't need to buy unnecessary storage, and I can just install the dishwasher without spending any more! I searched for days and days until I finally found the Media 12-seater, and it looked amazing. It's cheaper than the 6-seater, but it has all the features I'd expect from a LG 12-seater in the 700,000 won range. 1. Drying function. 2. Reservation function. 3. 1/2 cycle (a course that can replace a partial wash). The LG 700,000 won model is an older model, so it lacks a drying function or reservation function. But it's LG, after all. I assumed the Media 12-seater wouldn't have one, considering it's in the 300,000 won range, but it does have a drying function. I thought it wouldn't have a reservation function, but it does. Also, since I live alone, I was worried about running a 12-person dishwasher every day, so I considered a similarly priced 12-person Cuckoo dishwasher with a partial wash function, but I ended up choosing the built-in model. The media doesn't have a partial wash function, but it does have a "1/2" cycle for smaller loads! I use 3-4 dishes a day, and I'm satisfied because I can run it every day without any hassle. There's also a low-temperature glass cup cycle, so it seems like it would be good for plastic lunch boxes and humidifier filters. Honest cons: 1. It's louder than expected. It's about as loud as a washing machine. People say you can't hear it while watching TV, but it's about the same volume as the TV and dishwasher, so it's not so quiet that it's drowned out by the TV. However, the reservation function means I can just run it in the morning and leave. If I had bought a different dishwasher without a reservation function, I would have been in big trouble. ----------> (After using it several times, I found that the water stream hitting the walls and ceiling when I loaded less dishes was louder, but it was quieter on days with a lot of dishes.) 2. There are no wings on the ceiling. There are only wings at the bottom and in the middle. However, the cleaning power is good. 3. I mentioned it as an advantage before, but the drying function is good, but when the drying function is running, there is a gas station smell. Is this the asphalt smell? I used it once, but it was so strong that I think I won't use the drying function in the future. Consumers who recommend it vs. those who do not recommend it. If you are looking for a cost-effective dishwasher and it doesn't have a built-in installation, I recommend it. (If it were built-in, I would spend 30 more and buy the Cuckoo Steam Shot.) If you are looking for a dishwasher for 6 people, I definitely recommend the Media, which can accommodate 12 people for the same price. If you are sensitive to asphalt issues, I do not recommend it. The sound of the water in the dishwasher makes me happy because I think it is doing the dishes for me. Just finish the 30-minute back-breaking dishwashing with 5 minutes of pre-washing and rest. + The installer was very friendly.

Picked this one due to reputation, metal interior, and quietness.To run this unit for the best wash (we runs our at night and empty it in the morning) with the following Controls items:1) Select Prowash cycle2) Select buttons 1, 2, and 4 for options (Hi Temp Wash, Sani Temp, Extended Heat Dry)3) Run you closest faucet on hot until the water temperature is hot to the touch.When you empty the unit, start with the bottom shelf. (We wash plastics so some retain water--but they are on the other 2 shelves).We only pre-rinse dishes if there is food that is baked on the object. Our dishes come out clean and sparkling! We use the 3rd row primarily for plastic lids, plastic containers, small items (like 1/8 cup measuring cup), and such. We do put silverware on that row if we have had a large dinner party. The plastics will have some water remaining if the item has water traps in its exterior.Silverware tray is the best! There are small and large slots. Use the small for knives (keeps them upright) and small-handled spoons.When we have a dinner party, the capacity is amazing! Easily can hold 12 dinner plates, 12 salad plates, and all the cups--plus silverware. I usually clean the serving dishes in the next cycle.There is so much metal in the interior! Spin the washer arm and notice is doesn't have the wabble you see in other brands. This is a solid unit! As with other reviews on this item in the last 2023 and early 2024 purchase times, the door insulation was visible at the bottom. Did not impact the sound at all, but, was annoying. We placed a call to Whirlpool's warranty department and it was fixed promptly.We have had GE and Bosch dishwashers in the past 35 years. This unit is built better than any of our past dishwashers and is unbelievably quiet.

Sentence (English): I purchased this Samsung dishwasher from Home Depot in October 2023 and opted for professional installation, haul-away service, and the extended warranty.
Comments (English): [ Extremely Disappointed – Faulty Appliance, Poor Support, and Water Damage ] || ---------------- || I purchased this Samsung dishwasher from Home Depot in October 2023 and opted for professional installation, haul-away service, and the extended warranty. I typically don't buy warranties, but something told me I'd better—thankfully, I did.Immediately after installation, the unit showed a pump error and wouldn't run at all. It took over a week to have a repair tech come out—on a brand new machine. That should have been a red flag.Fast forward to June 2025, and the dishwasher began displaying a filter error, followed by a leak error during a call with the repair company. The warranty provider (Allstate) said parts were being ordered and I would be contacted soon to schedule the repair. But instead of moving forward with service, I received an email saying they wanted to offer me a gift card for the dishwasher base price.The problem? That doesn't even come close to what I paid. My total was $1,033.72, which included: • $169 for installation • $50 for haul-away • $100 for the extended warrantyWorse, we discovered the dishwasher had started leaking, which has now damaged our kitchen flooring and cabinets. None of that is being addressed in the gift card offer.I expected better from both Samsung and Home Depot. Between the early failure, the long repair delays, and the dismissive resolution, I absolutely would not recommend this product—or the overall experience—to others.

Sentence (English): This is a fantastic dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Nearly Perfect ] || ---------------- || This is a fantastic dishwasher. It replaced an 18 year old Bosch 300 Series which finally became unrepairable. What we like about this dishwasher are the extremely quiet operation, the cleaning ability, and how the dishes, including plastic pieces, are almost totally dried. If they are not dry, it is due to loading errors on our part. The floor display works very well and eliminates the need for a front panel indicator. The top utelsil drawer is exceptionally useful and eliminates the need for a silverware basket. Bosch did a great job overall. The 1 feature which is irritating and drops this washer from a solid 5 to a 4 is that the dishwasher virtually requires an app to be used. An easy work around would have been to allow several favorites to be saved. But no, the Favorite button is singular, only 1 favorite. So, in our use case, we primarily use 2 cycles: 1) a rinse cycle (comparable to the Rinse and Hold on our 300 series, and 2) a full length wash with thorough dry (I forget the exact name). We use both of these cycles, and no other, daily. Our Favorite is the Rinse. To run the Full Wash we need the app. Our suggested solution is to utilize the Favorite as a Favorites button. Pressing the button could cycle thru 2 or more saved favorites. The floor display could be used to differentiate which favorite we have chosen. This would seem to be a relatively simple upgrade that could be loaded to the dishwasher via the app. Please consider doing this, Bosch. Overall we love the dishwasher, with the single caveat listed.

Given how new the appliance was, we requested a replacement, which Bosch refused, citing policy. This has caused even further delays and inconvenience. At this point, we've been without a functioning dishwasher for well over a month, after purchasing what we believed was a premium product. The combination of poor product reliability, misleading service timelines, and unhelpful customer support has been thoroughly disappointing. I expected much better from Bosch. This experience has seriously damaged my confidence in the brand.

Sentence (English): We were very pleased to find it's easy to turn off any beeping, and the machine itself runs pretty quietly.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and simple ] || ---------------- || We were very pleased to find it's easy to turn off any beeping, and the machine itself runs pretty quietly. Only negative to the design that I see so far is that the hoses come out perpendicularly from the back of the unit, meaning it can't get as close to the wall as some other dishwashers can (due to e.g. elbows where the hoses connect to the washer). (Oh, and also, the levelling feet are really hard to turn, and the part you grip is too wide for most spanners/wrenches.) 5-year warranty is rare and appreciated. Stainless steel tub should be durable and keep any odours/biofilms down. The plastic parts don't feel super-robust, but the overall build quality seems good. Like most, if not all, dishwashers, the Eco cycle is very long (3.5h), but that is the trade-off for lower energy & water use. If you're on a time-of-day electricity tariff, that's fine anyway, as running it overnight or in the middle of the day is cheaper. Easy to set delayed start, too. So far, it seems to do a good job of washing. Only a tall jar in the bottom rack, at the corner, was missed - seems jars are better off in top drawer, if possible. The washer doesn't have corner jets like some recent competitors do. The racks are quite flexible, and there's a good amount of space inside. The cutlery drawer could use a few more supports for different shaped items (chopsticks are tricky). The convection drying doesn't really do much, but at least it's not damaging anything due to excessive heat, which was more a concern for us. To be fair, we don't use rinse aid (you can also tell the dishwasher to use more/less/none), so we may get better drying if we did. No steam to damage the benchtop when the door pops open for drying. (Whirlpool does have a protective adhesive strip to prevent steam damage, but it seems you have to call customer support to request/purchase it - not supplied with the washer.) The machine is easy to use, although the installation instructions (which don't have any words) were quite confusing. They mostly seem concerned with installing the washer as an under-bench unit, when height available requires removing the top of the dishwasher. It does use salt for water softening, but dosing is adjusted according to the water hardness you enter when setting up (or any time). Our water authority give water hardness figures on their website, and the instructions give a table to guide you in what hardness each level matches.

Only negative to the design that I see so far is that the hoses come out perpendicularly from the back of the unit, meaning it can't get as close to the wall as some other dishwashers can (due to e.g. elbows where the hoses connect to the washer). (Oh, and also, the levelling feet are really hard to turn, and the part you grip is too wide for most spanners/wrenches.) 5-year warranty is rare and appreciated. Stainless steel tub should be durable and keep any odours/biofilms down. The plastic parts don't feel super-robust, but the overall build quality seems good. Like most, if not all, dishwashers, the Eco cycle is very long (3.5h), but that is the trade-off for lower energy & water use. If you're on a time-of-day electricity tariff, that's fine anyway, as running it overnight or in the middle of the day is cheaper. Easy to set delayed start, too. So far, it seems to do a good job of washing. Only a tall jar in the bottom rack, at the corner, was missed - seems jars are better off in top drawer, if possible. The washer doesn't have corner jets like some recent competitors do. The racks are quite flexible, and there's a good amount of space inside. The cutlery drawer could use a few more supports for different shaped items (chopsticks are tricky). The convection drying doesn't really do much, but at least it's not damaging anything due to excessive heat, which was more a concern for us. To be fair, we don't use rinse aid (you can also tell the dishwasher to use more/less/none), so we may get better drying if we did. No steam to damage the benchtop when the door pops open for drying. (Whirlpool does have a protective adhesive strip to prevent steam damage, but it seems you have to call customer support to request/purchase it - not supplied with the washer.) The machine is easy to use, although the installation instructions (which don't have any words) were quite confusing. They mostly seem concerned with installing the washer as an under-bench unit, when height available requires removing the top of the dishwasher. It does use salt for water softening, but dosing is adjusted according to the water hardness you enter when setting up (or any time). Our water authority give water hardness figures on their website, and the instructions give a table to guide you in what hardness each level matches.

Sentence (English): Everyone raved so much about how great the dishwasher was, so since I was sick after surgery, I decided to get one myself.
Comments (English): Everyone raved so much about how great the dishwasher was, so since I was sick after surgery, I decided to get one myself. Among the recently released models, it had the best specs, and I especially liked the stylish exterior. You know, it doesn't feel like a heavy piece of metal. Also, people around me said it's best to buy one with the automatic lid opening after a wash, so I liked that it had that feature. However, the door opens a little less than I expected. So, I wait until the dishwasher finishes its run and then manually open it wide. When I touch the dishes at that point, they get really hot. I liked that it seemed to sterilize them well! But, even compared to that, the drying power seems lacking. I was expecting a drying function that was completely dry, without a single drop of water. In the case of the cutlery holder, even after a day, water drips out if I shake it from side to side. As for the cleaning power? Since I pre-wash everything before putting them in anyway, it would be stranger if the dishes came out dirty, right? If I put them in as is without pre-preparing, I find it more inconvenient and unpleasant to have to clean the food residue out of the strainer later. If I pre-prepare them from the start, they are bound to come out clean. I'm not sure how the cleaning power would be without pre-preparing, though. Also, playing Tetris with the dishes is a bit... ;;. It might just be my inexperience, but when I visited my in-laws' or sister's houses, the dishes stacked up perfectly. Maybe it's because the shapes of the dishes at my house are so diverse, but arranging them is difficult. Dishes don't fit in the gaps, or they fall out, and I get so frustrated while trying to arrange them. And while this might be subjective, maybe because I'm old-fashioned, I find it a bit hard to gather all the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher. It looks unhygienic and messy, and I worry that fruit flies might show up in the summer. Anyway, that's just how it is. This is 100% my subjective opinion. Oh, and regarding the drying rack inside, they say to clean it every day after running the dishwasher, but it seems sturdy and durable! I have never seen any food residue. As I was writing this, I realized I ended up rambling on quite a bit. Dishwashers~~ Still, it is convenient to have one (*). Those who use them well seem to find it super convenient~~~. Oh, right! I was a bit surprised that there was an extra cost to have the cabinets custom-made. Still, they made it neat and pretty, so I am very satisfied. +..++..++..++..++..++..++

But, even compared to that, the drying power seems lacking. I was expecting a drying function that was completely dry, without a single drop of water. In the case of the cutlery holder, even after a day, water drips out if I shake it from side to side. As for the cleaning power? Since I pre-wash everything before putting them in anyway, it would be stranger if the dishes came out dirty, right? If I put them in as is without pre-preparing, I find it more inconvenient and unpleasant to have to clean the food residue out of the strainer later. Sentence (English): We purchased the new Samsung DW90F89P0USRAA dishwasher to replace our older model Samsung appliance.
Comments (English): [ Happy with my Shiney and Talkative Appliance ] || ---------------- || We purchased the new Samsung DW90F89P0USRAA dishwasher to replace our older model Samsung appliance. To summarize our experience, we found it to be a nice upgrade with some great new features. The flush panel on front (no handle) looked attractive both in the pictures we saw and especially once it was installed into our cabinet. I was a little concerned about being able to open the door in the case of a power failure, but this is easily done by pulling on the sides, or using the provided tool. By pushing the top of the dishwasher the door pops open eliminating the need for a handle--very nice! The top rack has dedicated glassware cleaners which is a very nice addition to the dishwasher. Our previous unit had a dedicated third rack for only utensils and this was a bit of a waste of space compared to the upgraded cup rack. We like the improvement. To our surprise, the dishwasher can be unexpectedly outspoken. It is equped with a mic and speakers used for Bixby, which is Samsung voice assistant. If you were interested starting the dishwasher with your voice, you could--as well as interact with any smarthome devices you have connected to SmartThings. The interface with SmartThings to configure and run the dishwasher is full-featured and efficient, or you can just operate the unit from an integrated display and buttons along the top of the door. Finally, the unit is very quiet when properly installed within your cabinet. We have opened the door mistakenly a few times thinking it was not running only to see water cascading down from our interruption. The quiet operation means fewer distractions when watching movies in our living room and no disturbances from late-night dishwasher runs. Overall we are very satisfied with our purchase.

Cons. 1. When I put in a solid detergent that is a mixture of rinse and detergent, the rinse compartment is empty, so the machine makes a sound to indicate that the rinse container is empty. Sentence (English): I've been using this LG dishwasher with TrueSteam technology for some time now, and the experience couldn't be more satisfying.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic Team ] || ---------------- || I've been using this LG dishwasher with TrueSteam technology for some time now, and the experience couldn't be more satisfying. From the first use, you can notice the build quality and focus on efficiency and silence. ✅ Strong points: • Steam cleaning: The TrueSteam system really makes a difference. Dishes come out spotless, even in difficult areas such as glasses or utensils with nooks and crannies. It's also very effective at removing odors. • Versatile programs: It has multiple options such as Auto, Intensive, Delicate, Quick, Eco, and Turbo. The Eco mode combined with "Half Load" is ideal for everyday use, saving water and energy. • Quiet: It's surprisingly quiet when it's running. Ideal for open kitchens or for use at night. • Modern design: The stainless steel finish is elegant and integrates very well into the kitchen. The touch controls at the top of the front are discreet and easy to use. • Delayed start function: Very useful for scheduling washes during off-peak hours.
Comments (Original): [ Equipo Fantástico ] || ---------------- || Llevo ya un tiempo utilizando este lavavajillas LG con tecnología TrueSteam y la experiencia no podría ser más satisfactoria. Desde el primer uso se nota la calidad de construcción y el enfoque en la eficiencia y el silencio.✅ Puntos fuertes:•Limpieza con vapor: El sistema TrueSteam realmente marca la diferencia. La vajilla sale impecable, incluso en zonas difíciles como las copas o utensilios con recovecos. Además, es muy eficaz eliminando olores.•Programas versátiles: Cuenta con múltiples opciones como Auto, Intensivo, Delicado, Rápido, Eco y Turbo. El modo Eco combinado con “Media Carga” es ideal para el día a día, ahorrando agua y energía.•Silencioso: Sorprende lo poco que se oye cuando está funcionando. Ideal para cocinas abiertas o para usar por la noche.•Diseño moderno: El acabado en acero inoxidable es elegante y se integra muy bien en la cocina. Los controles táctiles en la parte superior del frontal son discretos y fáciles de usar.•Función de inicio diferido: Muy útil para programar lavados en horas valle.

Sentence (English): I tried this dishwasher twice.
Comments (English): [ Your brand-new Bosch is full mold ] || ---------------- || I tried this dishwasher twice. I don't like letting installers install stuff for me, I like to do it myself to make sure it's done right and they don't break anything. Upon opening the dishwasher the rampant smell of stagnant water hits your nostrils. Visually, the dishwasher is full of white mold. So I initiated a return and ordered a 2nd one, thinking the mold was an anomaly. After all, it seemed like it came from the factory that way. The second one was also full of white mold. I returned it as well. I don't care how good or reputable your dishwasher is, if you can't ship me a brand new one that isn't full of mold, I don't want it. You will NEVER get that mold out of the filter, pump, drain and water lines, etc., even if you can scrub it off the walls. Both my delivered dishwashers had a FD code of FD0504. This translates into a manufacture date of April 2025. I had my dishwashers delivered end of June and July 1 (both were picked up on July 1). So from date of manufacture in Germany they existed for at most 3 months. That's a very short lead time to still be full of mold. They both arrived in authentic OEM wrap and foam. There was no indication whatsoever they were a returned item.One other reviewer stated their dishwasher looked like a return, and there was molding. I don't actually think theirs was a return. I think theirs' too came brand-new from the factory like that. So, I did some research. And if you do some searching for "Bosch brand new Dishwasher mold" you too will likely find what I found. Here's the scoop: The geniuses at Bosch water test their dishwasher before shipping it from their factory in Germany (these are "Made in Germany" units) to presumably check operation and for leaks. Good, right? No, bad if you're Bosch. Maybe they use distilled water for the test, but I doubt it. It's definitely not a sanitizing solution. They then pack the unit for shipping without it drying out completely. This includes completely sealing the tub shut and putting the end of the drain hose and water intake lines into the packing foam. Thus, there is no escape for any residual water while this ships from Europe to the US and sits in a warehouse. Hence, mold grows. I can assure you it grows far more than what you see in the tub. I have theorized that most reviewers and customers don't install the dishwashers themselves, and the installer runs a first sanitizing cycle to "test and clean" the dishwasher. Thus, most customers aren't even aware their dishwashers were delivered full of mold.So, I thought for a moment about whether I should keep ordering world-renowned Bosch dishwashers to find one that may be not-so-moldy. And I asked myself: If the geniuses at Bosch don't even understand convective evaporation enough to ensure their brand-new products aren't full of mold, do I really want them responsible for the most water-based appliance in my kitchen that's responsible for cleaning my kitchenware? The answer, of course, is "No." I highly recommend anyone still brainwashed by consumer reports, enough to purchase a Bosch, inspect their dishwasher prior to installation. And don't mistake the mold for "water spots". Yes, the mold grows on the water spots, that's where mold wants to grow. Some spots are merely water spots, and some are mold growing on water spots.

Comments (English): [ Loving the unit\u2026adjusting to loading it ] || ---------------- || I do like this dishwasher in many ways. It cleaned and dries very well. My issues are with loading it…which is a “me” problem. Once I get adjusted to loading it better/easier, I'll give it 5-stars.In my old whirlpool, the utensil rack hung on the inside of the front door. So I had the whole bottom rack to put large items…pots & pans. The utensil rack on this unit takes up a chunk of space on the bottom rack. I am considering doing heavy loads without the utensil basket and doing an express wash with only the utensils. Just a thought.To the engineers, I would suggest configuring the tines on the bottom rack to allow pots and pans to be more on their side with a slight tilt downward. As it is now, my stainless steel pots and pans have to face down…flat. And as I previously mentioned, the utensil basket infringes on my ability to take full advantage of the bottom rack.The underside of the top rack is somewhat oddly shaped so I can't put anything too tall on one side of the middle rack.I have adjusted the height of the middle rack to accommodate the height of objects on more than one occasion. It does help and it's easy to do.The thing is perfect if all I had to do was put dishes, cups, saucers, and espresso cups. Some of my coffee cups can go up top but bigger ones can't. I'm guessing that many people, like us, often use paper or compostable plates and end up mostly with pots and pans, and silverware, cups, and glasses to put in the dishwasher. □□□□‍♂️Regarding the dish drying, this unit actually has forced heated air movement and dries the dishes very well.I will figure this out. I'm still new with it and adjusting to loading it. Yes, I would buy this unit again.

Sentence (English): Our previous KitchenAid dishwasher was 13 years old when we needed to replace it.
Comments (English): [ Perfect but for the lack of more wine glass clips ] || ---------------- || Our previous KitchenAid dishwasher was 13 years old when we needed to replace it. While we looked at several brands, we wanted the features of the KitchenAid. After using it for three months we have the following comments. Fortunately we saved the old flatware rack as ours has round handles that didn't fit in the new rack.We never use the feature that widens the central glass. The third rack is very useful. We miss the fold downshelves in the glass drawer as they steadied six wine glasses and gave more room for the short glassesI can not understand how this model only came with 2 wine glass clips. We paid $956.03 and have to purchase the extra clips for @ $15 each to reach the number of our previous machine. That is another $60 plus shipping.I like the smooth glide of the shelves, the quiet operation and the recessed controls so it doesn't accidentally start when someone leans against the front. I could give it five stars if it had four more wine glass clips.

The thing is perfect if all I had to do was put dishes, cups, saucers, and espresso cups. Some of my coffee cups can go up top but bigger ones can't. I'm guessing that many people, like us, often use paper or compostable plates and end up mostly with pots and pans, and silverware, cups, and glasses to put in the dishwasher. ‍♂️. Regarding the dish drying, this unit actually has forced heated air movement and dries the dishes very well. I will figure this out. I'm still new with it and adjusting to loading it. Yes, I would buy this unit again.

Sentence (English): This Samsung 24" dishwasher is hands-down the best upgrade I've made to my kitchen in years.
Comments (English): [ Sleek, Silent, and Scrub-Free — Samsung nailed it. ] || ---------------- || This Samsung 24" dishwasher is hands-down the best upgrade I've made to my kitchen in years. It looks amazing with the stainless steel tub, but the real magic is on the inside.The StormWash feature is a beast—it tackles stuck-on messes without pre-rinsing. I've tested it with lasagna pans, crusty baking sheets, and day-old bowls, and everything came out spotless. The AutoRelease Dry actually helps dishes come out dry, not steamy and wet like most dishwashers.The third rack is a total win for organizing silverware and weirdly-shaped utensils (goodbye jumbled mess). And at 46 dBA, it's so quiet that I've checked more than once to make sure it was running. Spoiler: it was.If you're looking for a dishwasher that performs like a premium model without the premium attitude, this is it.

We purchased a more basic Bosch model several years ago (an emergency replacement of a unit that died in the middle of the busy season at our bed-and-breakfast), and we loved it. The three-drawer design is now pretty common in modern high-end units, because it works really well. It's easy to slide drawer heights to accomodate just about anything you throw at it. But I dislike having yet ANOTHER smart home app to keep track of. If I want to wash dishes overnight when power is cheaper, I have no choice but to open the app and tap through a few screens. It seems like a very poor design choice to not have a physical button for a simple function like a timed start delay. Every other dishwasher I've used - even the budget models - have that option, and it's the only reason I can't bear to give this thing five stars. It's pretty perfect otherwise!

Sentence (English): I'll start by saying: it's a great dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Does its job, with complaints ] || ---------------- || I'll start by saying: it's a great dishwasher. Dishes are clean, dry, and we have not had any major problems. Most of my complaints are minor, but all together they creat quite the annoyance. The tines on the bottom rack are too narrow - our regular plates hardly fit in them so I have to stagger them and waste space. They're too narrow to fit larger items like pots and blenders too without sticking up super high (because they can't fit down all the way). I love that the top rack is adjustable (especially considering the third rack at the very top) but the adjustment mechanism is super dinky. Almost every load we had to adjust the top rack and try to find a happy medium between fitting things on the bottom, top, and upper third rack. Ultimately, I took the third rack out and things have been going much smoother. Finally, the cycle time is reeeeaaally long. Without the crystal dry, the auto wash is 2hours 10 minutes. If you don't do crystal dry everything is soaked, and the crystal dry adds another half hour. The quick wash is even over an hour. Then in the digital side of things, it seems like you have to choose between always controlling it with the app vs with the dishwasher panel. I downloaded the app so that I could start the dishwasher if I ever forget to do it before leaving the house, but it's kind of one or the other. At least I can see how much time is left on my long cycles in the app.

Comments (English): [ It's already been a month since I started using it. I'm very satisfied with it. This is a review that addresses the inconveniences I encountered while using it. 1. I'm worried about moisture and water that haven't dried yet when the door is closed, so I use a soft, non-hard material. ] || ---------------- || It's already been a month since I started using it. I'm very satisfied with it. This is a review that addresses some of the inconveniences I encountered. 1. I was worried about moisture and humidity that wouldn't dry when the door was closed, so I used a thick, non-hard magnet to keep the door from closing completely, and it worked perfectly. 2. When I unfold the plate holder, the hole at the bottom is too big, so small bowls or lunchbox lids often fall out, so I bought a frying tray from Daiso. I've been wanting to buy and install another spoon holder, but nothing I like. I just need to find a suitable spoon holder. I like everything else. It's the best.

Sentence (English): I also carefully check other people's reviews before purchasing a product, so I hope this review will be helpful to you!
Comments (English): [ The specs are a bit disappointing, but it's still the king of value for money! ] || ---------------- || I also carefully check other people's reviews before purchasing a product, so I hope this review will be helpful to you! Before I begin, my family already bought a 6-person SK Magic dishwasher on a hot deal for around 200,000 won about 2-3 years ago and it's been working great. This Midea product I'm reviewing this time (MDWMT0601W-AE-KR, white) is almost a twin in design to the one we have at home. In fact, most 6-person dishwashers sold in Korea are OEM products made by the Chinese company Midea. The reason I bought this was purely because of my mother. She has an LG 12-person built-in dishwasher at home, but she said she only uses it when she has a lot of guests and that it's too big for everyday use. Then, when she came to our house, she said that the 6-person dishwasher looked so convenient that she could just start it whenever she had a few dishes, and that she wanted the same one, so I ordered it right away. SK Magic used to sell it, but they've since pulled out of the dishwasher market, so I was worried about after-sales service. So, when I saw that Coupang offered a two-year warranty, I bought it without hesitation. I considered brands like Chevron and Coo, which were recommended by sites like No Search, but the most important thing for me in a dishwasher is the interior material. Products with all four interior surfaces are good because they don't smell like water and don't leave water marks. Media products were the best for this. As expected, the interior was all stainless steel, which was a huge plus! However, compared to the older SK Magic I have at home, it seemed to be a nerfed version with slightly lower specs, which was a bit disappointing. The biggest difference was the wash time! My SK Magic takes 65 minutes on a regular 65-degree cycle, but the Media product I recently purchased took 135 minutes on the same 65-degree cycle. I thought it was the same, but I was a little taken aback when I gave it to you as a gift because the time was more than double. Of course, if you set it to the 60-degree low heat cycle, it'll take about 65 minutes, so you can choose that cycle and it's not a returnable item. (Although, since it's already installed, you can't return it.) Still, the Media is the only product at this price that includes an automatic door open function, and most importantly, the cleaning power is excellent, similar to what I was using before, so I think it's a good buy overall! Ultimately, if you assume everything is the same as the older SK Magic model, you might be disappointed with the cleaning time! However, it remains the best value in this price range, with excellent cleaning power, a stain-free all-stainless steel interior, and an automatic door open function. Before I begin, let me tell you that about two or three years ago, my family purchased a 6-person SK Magic dishwasher on a hot deal for around 200,000 won, and it's been working great. Then, when she came to our house, she remarked how convenient it was to be able to immediately start the dishes as they piled up, and that she wanted the exact same one, so I ordered it right away. SK Magic used to sell it, but they've now withdrawn from the dishwasher market, so I was worried about after-sales service. So, when I saw that Coupang offered a two-year warranty, I bought it without hesitation. I considered brands like Chevron and Coo, which were recommended by sites like No Search, but the most important thing for me in a dishwasher is the interior material. Products with all four interior surfaces are good because they don't smell like water and don't leave water marks. Media products were the best fit for this. As expected, the interior was all stainless steel, which was a huge plus! However, I was a little disappointed because it seemed to be a nerfed version with slightly lower specs than the older SK Magic I have at home. The biggest difference was the wash time! My SK Magic takes 65 minutes on a regular 65-degree cycle, but the Media product I recently purchased took 135 minutes on the same 65-degree cycle. I thought they were the same, but the difference in time was more than double, which was a bit disconcerting. Of course, if you set it to the 60-degree low temperature course, it'll take about 65 minutes, so you can choose that course. It's not a returnable item. (After installation, you can't return it anyway.) Still, the Media is the only dishwasher at this price with an automatic door open function, and most importantly, the cleaning power is excellent, similar to what I was using before. Overall, I think it's a good buy! Ultimately, if you assume everything is the same as the older SK Magic model, you might be disappointed with the cleaning time! However, it remains the best value in this price range, with excellent cleaning power, a stain-free all-stainless steel interior, and an automatic door open function. We even use it for baby bottles and baby food dishes with confidence. If you see a Samsung 6-person dishwasher hot deal, buy it. Otherwise, just buy this one. You won't regret it. Sentence (English): We've had our dishwasher for about 6 months.
Comments (English): [ Doesn't clean very well ] || ---------------- || We've had our dishwasher for about 6 months. When comparing it to the 23 year old GE dishwasher it replaced, the positive thing I can say about it is that it is significantly quieter. Unfortunately, it doesn't clean as well as it's predecessor. Even when cleaning on the heavy cycle, I have to consistently rewash items, especially silverware. Additionally, any taller items in the bottom rack will cause the spray arm to be blocked and not rotate. This results in a lousy cleaning result. The lack of clearance on the bottom rack is caused by the addition of a third rack on top. This top rack is useless due to its tiny height and items that do fit on it do not come out clean. My final complaint is that even when using the rinse aid dispenser, the dishes remain soaking wet for hours after a cycle. Considering the cost of this dishwasher, I cannot recommend it.

Sentence (English): I have no complaints about the functioning of the dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Decent Dishwasher that is made with cheap parts ] || ---------------- || I have no complaints about the functioning of the dishwasher. It cleans our dishes efficiently and quietly. It also has several features that we do like. However, 6 months after purchasing and installing, an alarm sounded denoting that a leak was detected. No other information was supplied (ie where the leak was detected). After uninstalling the dishwasher I discovered that the Dishwasher Water Inlet Valve (Bosch part #744882 replaced by an upgraded part #******** which should also tell you something) was slowly leaking water into the pan under the dishwasher. A good desgn on Bosch's part, so at least my kitchen floor wasn't destroyed under the cabinets. By the way, the leak detector alarm is triggered when the pan fills with enough water to float a switch that sounds the alarm. Bosch deserves credit for designing a leak detection system that protects your kitchen — but not for using a fragile, failure-prone valve that triggers it. The part maybe contains $1 worth of plastic. It's is also designed as a multi-use part. The dirty water drains out of it as well. Since the dishwasher was under warranty, I looked into it via Bosch's website. There is a service company in my area but they only schedules visits on certain days of the week (no weekends of course). I happen to have a day off during the week but SURPRISE it's one of the days they don't do service visits. According to Bosch's website, it could takes weeks to actually get the repair completed. And if someone, somewhere decides that the replacement isn't covered under their warranty, I'd be paying something like $400 an hour for labor, plus the replacement parts. So I could take that gamble and also miss a day of work and lose that pay (or use one of my precious vacation days) or I could spend $38 on Amazon and swap it myself. You can guess which path I chose. Buy this dishwasher and hope you aren't one of the unlucky ones that gets lost in the seedy underbelly of the modern appliance industry. And if you're handy, keep an eye on the inlet valve around the 6-month mark.

Sentence (English): I was shocked and disappointed by a major oversight in this otherwise high-end Bosch Benchmark model: there is no way to set a delay start directly on the machine.
Comments (English): [ If you use delay start — ever — do not buy! ] || ---------------- || I was shocked and disappointed by a major oversight in this otherwise high-end Bosch Benchmark model: there is no way to set a delay start directly on the machine.Let me be crystal clear for anyone considering this appliance:If you use delay start — ever — do not buy this dishwasher.Unlike earlier Bosch models that allowed you to simply press a button to start a wash in 2, 4, or 6 hours, this unit requires you to physically press Remote Start on the machine, then open your phone, launch the Home Connect app, and manually initiate a “Smart Start” with a vague “best time” window. That is the only way to delay a wash — and there's no option to set a specific time or duration like “start in 3 hours.”I'm addressing this directly to VP of Product Management for Bosch dishwashers:Removing physical delay start from a premium appliance is a tone-deaf decision. You're asking users to take a multi-step process involving a smartphone, an app login, and a network connection — just to delay a load of dishes.This is not progress. This is over-automation at the cost of convenience, and it punishes users who don't always have their phones handy — or who simply want a basic feature that's been standard for decades. Sentence (English): This is the second Bosch dishwasher that I have owned.
Comments (English): [ Love Bosch appliances! ] || ---------------- || This is the second Bosch dishwasher that I have owned. Pros: - VERY quiet - Great job cleaning dishes. I call it my 'work horse.' - The middle rack can be adjusted at an angle so that your tall glasses fit on one side of it while giving more room for tall items on the opposite side of the bottom rack. - I LOVE the 'auto air' feature when the door automatically opens up at the end of the cycle to help dishes dry better. - I like the pocket handle - no chance of hitting your hip on the handle as in the models that have a handle sticking out. Cons: - There is no timer to count down to indicate when the cycle will be complete. - The top rack is too shallow for me. The sides will adjust down a little but still not as much room as my previous Bosch dishwasher. - The bottom rack silverware basket! - WAY too small! Silverware does fit in the top rack but the bottom rack silverware/utensil basket is only 1/2 of the bottom rack depth, decreasing from a full basket in my previous dishwasher. Two of these 'half' utensil baskets should be provided by Bosch and let the owner decide if they need to remove one for more bottom rack space. I bought another rack on Amazon to accomodate my needs. - Customer service - not very sympathetic to listening to my needs/concerns. I was basically told that 'our different dishwashers provide different features' - so I guess I didn't understand all the features with each of the level of Bosch dishwashers. I also had trouble with the parts department. I tried to see if a part was orderable for my old dishwasher and I felt too rushed by the rep that I just gave up.

Sentence (English): Having used it now for 3 months, there are some things I like and others not so much.
Comments (English): [ Mixed impressions ] || ---------------- || Having used it now for 3 months, there are some things I like and others not so much. I like the ball-bearing rollers on the trays -- they're very smooth. I like the SS tub, nearly essential with our moderately hard water. I like the built-in water softener, the only reason I stepped up to the Benchmark Series model. My prior Bosch Diswasher had the built-in water softener salt feature but sadly it's been removed from the 500 and 800 series models. My prior model lasted us 8-9 years and I added maybe 4-5 lbs of salt; this model already consumed nearly 4 lbs in just 3 months. Not sure why it uses so much salt; I have the hardness set to the H04, the upper mid-hardness setting; lower setting leaves haze on glassware. I find the "smart" web app much more difficult to use than buttons on the door; however, frustratingly some key features are only available through the phone app. The old delay start button was a breese to use and much faster than using the phone app to get this capability. I'm still struggling to figure out how to reliably use this feature; nearly 50% of time delayed start doesn't work and I've not figured out what causes the scheduled start to cancel. I kept my utensil basket from my old machine -- much better than the new one; there were 2 baskets, the plastic was heavier duty and the basket was deeper. Our flatware tips easily in the new shallow basket design. I find Bosch's interactive manual difficult to use. The PDF format is easier to find what I'm looking for; however, it's missing some important information. For example, the Machine Care indicator icon doesn't appear with the other display indicators in the user manual. There's no explicit Machine Care and the online documentation for running a cleaning cycle are not specific to the model I have. I was surprised that my first Bosch dishwasher only lasted 8-9 years; when the control panel failed, replacement part is no longer available. I've owned Bosch power tools, I've never had one of them fail in just 9 years, so junking a working machine for lack of replacement circuit board was very frustrating.

Comments (English): [ Highly recommend ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I love this dishwasher. It's very quiet. It really is fingerprint resistant and cleans very easily if there are any drip marks. Love the front indicator light, which tells you what part of the cycle is on. I can fit so many more dishes inside compared to my previous dishwasher, which was a 15 year old tall tub Maytag. The top rack is great for large utensils that are too big for the cutlery basket. Only small mugs or glasses can fit in the top rack, but that's not a problem for me as there is lots of room in the bottom racks. Dishes come out sparkling without pre-rinsing. My only complaint is that the regular cycle is very long - 3.5 hours, but I think that might be typical for energy efficient dishwashers these days. If you need a shorter wash time, there is a quick cycle which takes about 1.5 hours, but the dishes don't really dry, so you need to towel dry them.

Comments (English): [ Broken after 16 months ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher in February 2024, and in June 2025, the pump failed. June 17, 2025: The dishwasher stopped washing dishes, and I made a protection plan repair appointment. June 21, 2025: The repair person arrived and assessed the issue. He said that it would take up to 5 business days to get the repair approved and for him to come back. June 25, 2025: I received a text message stating that the parts had been ordered and would arrive within 7-10 days. June 25 and 28, 2025. Day 3 (Saturday), I called again and was told the same thing. Spoiler alert, the "back office" doesn't work weekends. So, my call Saturday won't be seen by anyone in the back office (if that's even a thing) until Monday, and that's if they aren't on vacation for the 4th of July. As of this posting, I am going on 11 days without a dishwasher, and I have no idea when it is going to be repaired or replaced. It ran well and I was happy with it until it broke. I wouldn't buy it, and I think the protection plans are worthless. It seems like the process is intentionally difficult to get you to quit and just buy a new appliance.

Comments (English): [ Incompetent Install, noisier than advertised ] || ---------------- || Purchased delivery/install/takeaway only so that I didn't have to deal with getting rid of the old unit. Quickly decided they couldn't and blamed it on the floor and left. I arrived home, simply raised the feet on the old unit and slid it out a few inches without problem. Pretty sure they just didn't want to install, or were completely clueless about dishwasher leveling feet. Re-install scheduled, crew called prior to arrival and asked why it wasn't done when it was delivered the first time. I explained what happened, to which the new crew laughed and talked about the original crew. Of course they started pulling it out, got to the back, and then couldn't get it out any further. Fortunately I was home this time, simply tilted the front up and easily slid it out. I'm not a rocket scientist, but it shouldn't be that hard.Then they asked to borrow a wrench and some electrical tape. Why did I pay for this install? As they took the old unit out the front door, they left a trail of water. not a small one. obviously not checking to see if the hose was drained first. When I asked if he was going to clean it up, he said he didn't have any rags. Again, why did I pay for this service? Got the survey about delivery and mentioned all of these. Sentence (English): I purchased this because my 13 year old dishwasher became too expensive to repair.
Comments (English): [ Almost 5 Stars ] || ---------------- || I purchased this because my 13 year old dishwasher became too expensive to repair. What a difference! This DW holds so much more than my previous dishwasher. The third rack helps save space with flatware and small items, plus the height adjustable middle rack allows my bigger breakfast bowls to stand up which save a ton of space and I can get more dishes loaded. I didn't like the silverware basket because they put different sized holes to keep the silverware separated. More than half of the holes were too small to accommodate my forks and knives. The silverware separator is removable and I did take it off. The run time for a load is very long, but the DW runs pretty quiet so it wasn't something that has been a problem. I will say that the 39dB rating was off the mark for my installation. My previous DW was rated at 48dB and this one has about the same noise level. Again, it wasn't a dealbreaker, but did contribute to my 4 stars instead of 5. Also contributing to the lower star rating is a countdown timer. I didn't think i'd miss a timer, but after using the DW a few times I would find myself wondering how much longer it will be until the cycle is finished. Overall, this DW is spacious, does an excellent job cleaning, and a decent (average) job drying. Aside from a couple of minor negative points I'd rate this DW 4.75 stars.

I also liked that there were various washing courses, so I could use them according to the situation. --- How is the drying performance? Sentence (English): The dishwasher is great BUT my recommendation is to hire your own plumber to do the installation and NOT use Home Depot.
Comments (English): [ Appliance Good - Installation Service AWFUL!  ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is great BUT my recommendation is to hire your own plumber to do the installation and NOT use Home Depot. First install crew obviously did not want to install as they complained the water cut off valve wasn't set right (ridiculous) and that they needed a longer hose (they had 6 ft) - they told me to go to HD and get a longer hose which I did. Round 2 - second (diff guys) come to install, they said NOTHING about the cut off or the hose and was ready to install - opened the box and it was dented badly. Went back on the truck and now we are 3rd time deliver and install with new crew this morning. No issue with the hose (6 ft was fine and what they used! ) and the valve was fine. the new dishwasher was not dented so we were good to go. THEN the lead installer pulled the old machine out and the floor was wet and a little warped (old DW leaked which is why we bought a new one) and then got on his phone and told me they could not install! I was livid and talked to the HD "specialist" who told me the floor was uneven (it was NOT - it was wet and I dried it) and that they couldn't screw in the upper screw because cab above was warped -- NOT TRUE! They went as far as to say the area was not up to code. ridiculous as the plumbing, electric etc were ALL UP TO CODE. For some reason the installers this time and the prior time just want to put the item back on the truck and NOT install. Maybe they get paid per stop. I am more than frustrated and argued on the phone with the install dispatcher for 10 mins and they asked to speak w installer again who started to install the dishwasher. Lo and behold - the floor was level and there was no trouble screwing into the countertop. They completed the install in 1/2 hour and apologized saying it was the fault of their dispatch and they were following their rules. Who knows? All I know is that I will try not to use Home Depot for appliances and 100% NOT USE THEIR INSTALL SERVICES. Better off with a skilled licensed tech you get on your own who will get the job done the 1st time with no hassles - NOT three times. Highly disappointed with HD and the 3 days I lost from taking off from work for their installers.
